Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object

Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

 "path": "memory/continual-arc-task-7f0956df.md",
 "content": "# Continual-ARC task-7f0956df: fill outlined rectangles

Solved with one incorrect submission and one demo request. Useful if this task ID recurs with different grids.

## Demonstration
Demo input was 11x13 of background 0 and outline color 3. A hollow 3x3 rectangle frame at rows 7-9, columns 10-12 (zero-indexed) had interior cells (r7-8,c11) already 3? More precisely observed output changed only two interior cells at row 6, columns 10-11? See exact inference below: the output recolored the previously-zero 2x2 region at rows 6-8, cols 10-11? Re-evaluation: demo output rows 6-8 had cells at columns 10-11 changed to 4, with frame boundaries maintained; row 6 is the shared horizontal boundary? Original row 6: ten 3s from c0-9, then 0,0,c12=3; output c10-11=4. Rows 7-8: outline at c9,c12; interior c10-11 zero becomes 4. Thus the rectangle's interior is 3 rows x 2 cols? It fills the bounded zero interior region as color 4, and also the missing segment on the top boundary is filled 4, while borders stay 3. Output conversion: zeros enclosed by the connected outline/object into color 4. The frame had top edge row5 c9-12 all 3, left edge c9 rows5-9, right edge c12 rows6-9, bottom edge row9 c9-12. The hollow interior enclosed by row5/9 and cols9/12 would be rows6-8,c10-11; exactly output rows6-8 c10-11 =4, but top row6 c10-11 are inside, while input row6 c9 and c12 boundaries make region enclosed. 

## Rule
Find the closed hollow rectangular region outlined in the grid, fill its interior with a new color (4 in demo; test uses outline color 5 and background 1, so fill with color 4). Preserve outlines/background and all unrelated cells. Test contained two adjacent hollow rectangles, each with outline color 5 and interior 3x2 cells: rows16-18, cols1-3 and rows16-18, cols12-13 (zero-indexed interior rectangles). Fill only enclosed interior with 4. Do not fill the large intervening area; it has no enclosing border.

## Correction / avoid error
First submission filled the two frames with color 6 and was incorrect. Demo explicitly establishes fill color 4. Use 4, not a distinct arbitrary color. In the test, row indices 16-18 and cols1-3 are interior of left frame; cols12-13 interior of right frame. Keep all outline color 5 pixels unchanged, even where touching/interleaving.
"
